analysis: The supplied units are BASE-side text of ProviderLoop.swift (lines 1-1116). The patch excerpt shows head changes only to stored-state declarations in the actor: autopilotHistory becomes a labeled tuple with an added `detail` field, and new in-memory state is added (autopilotAdoptedModelIDs, autopilotHolds, autopilotBusyClock, transitionWatchdog, autopilotStalledCommandId, startupPreloadStopRequested, and further fields truncated at line ~380). These are internal actor properties for autopilot placement and a transition watchdog. They have no direct effect on the security boundaries visible here: the coordinator WebSocket (TB-002), E2E key handling (A-003), attestation signing, or the SSD prefix cache (T-041). The X25519 key is still generated per process (NodeKeyPair.generate(), line 833), and the attestation signer path is unchanged. The excerpt was truncated, so the new `detail` string and the watchdog/hold logic are not fully visible. The behavior of the companion files (ProviderLoop+AutopilotPlacement etc.), including where `detail` is populated and whether it could carry sensitive data into coordinator-visible status, was not supplied. The integration pass should check: (1) whether autopilot `detail` strings or the watchdog cancel path leak prompt-derived data or model identity beyond what heartbeats already expose; (2) whether the watchdog cancelling startup preload (startupPreloadStopRequested) or in-flight operations can bypass a self-test or weight-hash gate (T-027, failedSelfTestHashes) or leave a model advertised without the load gate; (3) whether autopilotAdoptedModelIDs, which keeps models serving after the lease, respects the advertised-set and weight-hash checks. No concrete security regression is evidenced in the supplied lines; those items are unverified contracts, so needs_deeper_review is set.
